statements.impact_statement: GHSA-r7wm-3cxj-wff9 is the incomplete-fix follow-up to GHSA-72hv-8253-57qq: it extends the same maxNumberLength bypass to the chunked-feed integer-digit path of jackson-core's non-blocking async parser (NonBlockingUtf8JsonParserBase), where a maliciously chunked stream can accumulate digits up to maxStringLength before validation fires. As with the parent advisory, the affected jackson-core copy is bundled inside the OpenTelemetry Java agent shipped from smart-caches-core on the 1.33.6 line and is used only for instrumentation. Only the non-blocking async parser is affected (createNonBlockingByteArrayParser / createNonBlockingByteBufferParser); the synchronous parsers used in our applications are not. We do not expose Jackson's async parser to attacker-controlled JSON in this image, so the vulnerable code path is not exercised.

Applies to jackson-core 2.22.0 as pulled in directly by applications built on the Smart Caches parent 1.0.0 line (the version Trivy reports against jackson-core-2.22.0.jar). GHSA-r7wm-3cxj-wff9 affects only jackson-core's non-blocking async parser (createNonBlockingByteArrayParser / createNonBlockingByteBufferParser); a full codebase review found no use of the non-blocking parser anywhere in our applications, which parse exclusively via the synchronous parsers over servlet/JAX-RS request bodies, not reactive chunked streams. The vulnerable code path is therefore not reachable. This statement lists the exact PURL so it matches under Trivy's native OpenVEX (product-identifier) matching as well as Grype's; the durable remediation is the upgrade to jackson-core 2.22.1 via Smart Caches parent 1.0.3.
